newsitem.title: HONG KONG: JAL get the birds for UN Palais.
newsitem.headline: JAL get the birds for UN Palais.

text.p: Five Japanese peacocks took to the skies aboard a JAL flight from Tokyo on Thursday to add a splash of new colour to the United Nations, a Japan Airlines press statement said.

The birds are gifts from a Japanese natural history park, the Izu Saboten Park in Shizouka Prefecture, to help replace a flock of peacocks which grace the UN headquarters at the Palais Des Nations in Geneva. When the building was donated to the city 106 years ago, the donor stipulated peacocks should always be on parade.
But old age, illness and hungry foxes has cut numbers from 15 to just three males.
To make four new couples, the four female peahens and one peacock are being flown free of charge by JAL from Tokyo to Zurich before being taken to their new home.

The colourful gift is supported by the Japanese Foreign Ministry and the Japanese embassy in Geneva to mark Japan's 40th anniversary of joining the UN, JAL added. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
